title: OWASP Threat Dragon and pytm, by the risk it changes
summary: Two OWASP threat-modelling tools: Threat Dragon draws data-flow diagrams with their threats and remediations, and pytm generates them from a description of the system written as code. Like a behaviour policy, a threat model changes nothing about what the agent can reach. It can replace *nobody knows* with an answer, as far as the people drawing it know the system.

baseline.why: The model's typical deployment, with the answers this project addresses stated as they are without it: nobody knows what it could reach at full speed.

does.text: Threat models as data-flow diagrams, with threats and remediations.
does.quote: Threat Dragon provides an environment to create threat models as data-flow diagrams, along with associated threats and remediations.

changes.why: The weakest mapping on this page, stated as such: neither tool discovers reach; the answer is only as good as what the people drawing the model know. For the typical deployment the answer is customer-facing.

basis.quote: Threat Dragon provides an environment to create threat models as data-flow diagrams, along with associated threats and remediations.

adds_note: Threat Dragon stores models in a repository or a drive the deployer chooses, so it needs a credential for that store. A threat model is a document: it goes out of date the day the deployment changes unless somebody keeps it.
adoption: Draw one agent in one deployment, not the architecture in general: the tools, the credentials and what each reaches.
Keep the model beside the deployment and change it when the deployment changes.
Customise the threat library for agents: the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications is the obvious place to start.
does_not_claim: That a diagram retires a risk by itself. It names reach; it bounds nothing.
That it was tested. Nothing was installed or run; every change rests on the documentation quoted beside it.
next: Published, and sent to the project's maintainers at the same time. If a change is wrong, or another answer should move, the case changes with the date they said so.
